paper.title_en: Super-resolution quantum imaging via multiphoton correlation
paper.abstract_en: The resolution of conventional imaging is fundamentally constrained by the diffraction limit. Here we demonstrate that this limit can be overcome using classical thermal light, through the correlation of multiphoton subsystems. By resolving the photon numbers detected in the two arms of a Hanbury Brown-Twiss interferometer, the correlation function exhibits a narrowed peak or dip whose width is tunable via the average photon number. Temporal and spatial super-resolution enhancements up to 11.8-fold and 5.1-fold, respectively, are experimentally achieved. As a proof-of-principle experiment, a double-pinhole that is completely unresolved by standard ghost imaging becomes clearly distinguishable via the correlation of two-photon versus zero-photon. The principle of this super-resolution imaging can be interpreted as a combination of classical super-resolution imaging and quantum super-resolution imaging. This work provides a versatile platform for super-resolution imaging and lithography, and opens a new avenue for exploring the boundary between classical and nonclassical phenomena.
